short: Timur's son turned a conqueror's spoils into a settled Persianate sultanate at Herat.
full:
Shah Rukh had governed Khorasan from Herat since 1397 and was the least warlike of Timur's surviving sons. The succession dissolved into war on his father's death in 1405; he secured Khorasan first, then took Samarkand from his nephew Khalil Sultan in 1409, and by 1420 held everything east of western Iran. He kept his court at Herat rather than moving to Samarkand, which he gave to his son Ulugh Beg.

He also abandoned the legal fiction his father had needed. There was no more puppet Chagatayid khan; Shah Rukh ruled in his own name as sultan and padishah, and grounded his authority in Islamic legitimacy and the patronage of scholars rather than in Genghisid descent. He exchanged embassies with the Yongle Emperor, one of which produced Ghiyath al-Din Naqqash's detailed account of Ming China, and his wife Gawhar Shad built the mosque at Mashhad and the complex at Herat. He died in March 1447 near Rayy, and the empire immediately began to come apart.
